jaredklewis · Nov 28, 2026

I think it is fine as long as the founder/coder/whoever is just using the feedback as a source for ideas, not as the criteria for evaluating if the ideas are good or not.

Six years or so back I was experimenting with Elixir. I never ended up using it for anything important, but I still remember marveling at the wonderful personality of Jose Valim as I learned about Elixir. He was accessible on all kinds of channels like github, stack overflow, irc, and such, and he just exuded an openness to feedback. It seemed to me he was constantly interacting with Internet strangers about their ideas for Elixir. He always came off as very friendly and encouraging; I can never remember him being defensive or dismissive. Despite that, my impression was that Valim did not seem inclined to implement almost any of these ideas. He seemed to have a strong vision for what Elixir should be and passed on almost everything. Sometimes ideas were directly incorporated into Elixir, but mostly I think the effects of the feedback were indirect.

Another language I experimented with around that time (and again never used for anything important) was Elm. Elm's founder engaged with unsolicited feedback very differently. The contrast between the two approaches made a huge impression on me.

It's a real thing on mobile, where gameplay ideas get cloned the moment someone runs a big stack of ads showing them off.

Among the PC/console indies? I'm not aware of a lot of instances of this actually happening.
